Your main heal will be r4 Healing Touch with regrowth/ns + r11 Healing Touch for burst healing on tanks. It also has Natural Weapons to help land sleep/roots in ZG/AQ20/BWL.

Tree of Life builds gimp movement and shoehorn you into hot healing. The other viable builds are HOTW spec or Moonglow.

Gear: do not focus on collecting Heart of the Wild set. Focus on prebis with +healing https://www.wowhead.com/classic/guide/druid-healing-pre-raid-best-in-slot-bis-gear-wow-classic Keep in mind twow has unique items that can fill in as main/optional prebis as well.

author: Billy
content:
All of the druids specs have a niche role.

I run 19/11/21 which is a twow take on what StormX, Final Flash/Cucker etc. have run in the past.  It's strength is killing potential at range, using feral charge for gap closer, interrupt, escapes in 1v2 etc. while still having NS heal. It's *very* gear dependent as well. https://talents.turtle-wow.org/druid/P0X08I-UK06-ZW301 Vengeance/Natural Shapeshifter are flex points but Vengeance is nice if you can manage mana for shifting.

HOTW is based around similar flexibility as 19/11/21  https://talents.turtle-wow.org/druid/1-UK193EDO-ZW301 You will typically kill a bit slower as HOTW and be spending more time in bear/cat. Survivability can be higher in this build. You will be lacking Natural Weapons 3/3 for +hit. So you *will* need to get some hit on gear. HOTW is also a great choice if you like to do attrition fights to run people out of resources. It still has NS heal for self emergency or saving a teammate. I recommend keeping the 1 point in Nature's Grasp... 2/2 Feline Swfitness or 5/5 Heart of the Wild are flex points if you so choose instead.

Moonglow is basically a better healer with more mana conservation sources and more caster dps. However, the other two specs also conserve mana by sitting in bear to build mana back up so it's a trade. You will also lack Feral Charge which is imo one of the most useful druid abilities.

TLDR: 
19/11/21 -  for more caster dps with versatility.
HOTW - versatility + more survivability + more melee potential.
Moonglow - for focusing only on balance/resto, lacks Feral Charge for offensive/defensive options. 

Cheers.

author: Elesion
content:
I haven't done proper PvP in a long time but as a fairly old-school player I used to run a feral/resto hybrid build. My Blood Ring build was a homebrew 9/21/21. I too feel that hybrids are not nearly as strong as in Vanilla, but as gretchen mentioned mostly because pure feral is just so much stronger in a burst meta on TWoW (both due to mechanical/talent changes and because of lots of better gear).
It usually is a balancing act (as it probably should be). I've ended up 1 on 1 in BR a few times against other druids and my hybrid build (with mixed healing/tank gear) always won handily against deep feral because of better mana regen and more instant heals (time out of bear form is very dangerous). Rogues/warriors any druid should be able to eat for breakfast. But against casters deep feral does seem to have an edge. That's why I mixed in Berserk instead of Omen, for a little bit of burst at the opener and a second fear break.
And I totally don't agree that druids are bad pvp healers. We have the best mobility by far and the least chance of getting interrupted (counter spell, kick, pummel, earth shock) just because of our amazing arsenal of instant casts. Poly doesn't bother us, fear can be broken by trinket or Berserking, Blind can be abolish countered. Between keeping Reju on everyone, Swiftmend, Nature's Swiftness, 21s HoT from Regrowth... you can just run around like a madman keeping everyone topped off barely ever stopping to actually cast something. With Swiftmend and NS your ability to react to dangerous burst is unrivalled. If the enemy ignores you, they lose because you heal your team. If the enemy focusses you, they lose because you go bear or travel form. The ability to turn from the squishy healer into the tankiest target on the battlefield at the press of a button is huge. Druids might be the best PvP healers imo.

author: Elesion
content:
It's not bad, Swift Travel Form is just almost useless.
__Advantages:__ You're immune to polymorph, you can use it to fake a heal spell and bait an interrupt, you can pre-cast it on a boat, it looks great, it comes from a sweet questline, you can use it to herb.
__Disadvantages:__ Same drawbacks as a mount (3s cast time, only outside, only out of combat) while not getting any mount speed bonuses (spurs, gloves enchant, trinkets) making it worse than plainsrunning, not even the PvP set bonus applies (which is specifically aimed at animal forms), it comes fairly late (palas and warlocks do their epic mount quest pre-raid while we need to full-clear ES - by that time in character progression most people probably have bought journeyman riding).
So yeah... do it for PvP or flavor, but for actual everyday travel you'll still be using a mount. My preferred fix would be make it instant cast like all other forms and disable it in battlegrounds (like plainsrunning), keep the out-of-combat requirement. Then it would be awesome for short distances and I would use it all the time.

author: Elesion
content:
Just like with your statements on bears I would seriously implore you to get some hands-on experience in raids with the spec before making sweeping statements.
°) Powershifting is not a build, it's a tool that synergizes with all builds. Think of it as a button that says "spend 1 GCD, receive 60 energy".
°) Thus claw/bleed is not an alternative to powershifting. It's an alternative to shred/FB. Powershifting helps both. The only alternative to powershifting that TWoW has ever attempted was buffing Tiger's Fury.
°) Claw/bleed runs into severe issues early on in your raiding career when you discover that half the stuff in MC is immune to bleed effects. And by your own admission claw/bleed is tuned to be worse than shred/FB. So if you should learn shred/FB for MC anyway, why not stick with it?
°) Claw/bleed makes every single cat take up 2-3 debuff slots. That is fine for casual raids, but there will come a point where you take up a lot of debuff real estate for a spec tuned to not do the best dps you could. Raid leaders will think twice about bringing a claw/bleed cat.
There is no reason to doom about claw/bleed. I'm glad it exists as an alternative and as a leveling build. For casual and low-level raids nobody will even police your skill usage to the granularity where they would notice which build you run as a cat. But for serious endgame raiding I think a warning that claw/bleed has some serious draw-backs is well deserved.

content:
hey! so ive tried testing out a "pure" HT/Moonglow spec quite a bit ever since CC2 dropped but I've found it to be a bit underwhelming for anything other than tank healing.
https://talents.turtle-wow.org/druid?points=oAKYYKAYAIAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAFApADIDEIQFAAAA= this is the build i've ended up using mostly. It's Regrowth/NG but I still spec into Aessina's Bloom and I run 3/5 T2.5 + ZG trinket for both raid and tank healing. Most of the time im raid healing with Regrowth and tank healing with HT, but whenever I see a low raid member who already has a Regrowth active I'll use HT instead, this happens a lot more often if you have multiple druids in your raid like you said. You can even use r3 HT since Aessina's doesn't care about scaling coefficient. Last raid I healed (where I topped meters) was MC where Regrowth was around 60% of my healing and HT around 30%
An important thing to note is that T2.5 5/5 is bugged atm ( https://turtle-wow.org/bug-report?id=11613 ) so there's no point in using more than 3/5 (i use head, chest, boots), hopefully it'll get fixed at some point.
Unless more changes are made to Resto I think this is the future of HT, more of a situational spell in another spec rather than its own, standalone build.

author: FishyFish ><((('>
content:
My personal journey looked like this: 
Note* I enjoy all druid specs, so your milage may vary. Twow made me fall in love with Balance.
1-20, Balance
20-40, Balance or Resto, you can heal (Healing Touch Rank 4, Moonglow[Balance talent, lets you clearcast and makes healing as balance a breeze] + Rejuv [whatever your highest rank available] perfectly fine pre-40 as balance without having to acquire armor sets for each.
40+ Picked a spec to main. Gear it, and keep an Off-spec.

Your journey might look like this:
1-20 Balance, Use Entangle to 1v2 or 3 and solo elites  (https://talents.turtle-wow.org/druid?points=BgAaAIAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA=)
20-40, Feral, decide if u want to level as a cat, bear, or both. Fastest method is Front-Shredding as a Cat, but dungeons as bear are super fast too. https://talents.turtle-wow.org/druid?points=BgAaAIAAAAAAAAFAYYBYDCAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA=

after 40 get 5 points in Furor (resto tree), decide if u like cat or bear more I guess, Open wounds, Blood Frenzy, Improved Shred, Feral Adrenaline, Savage Fury, all benefit cat. Primal Fury (cat/bear).

After you should have enough to close out with Heart of the Wild>Leader of the Pack, and maybe Ancient Brutality (cat/bear).

Hope that helps. Also if you enjoy Cat/Bear, learning to Front Shred can speed up your kill times and out-of-combat down time, but if it isn't fun, Tiger Fury and combo your way to victory.

author: Alfras
content:
This is critical! We really need Open Wounds to only cost 2 talent points. With Furor and Omen of Clarity still being mandatory picks, Feral Cats are left with 1 talent point short for their DPS build in the Feral tree.

Due to the existence of bleed-immune mobs, the new Cat still cannot give up powershifting, which makes Furor essential. Omen of Clarity is a must-have for any Feral Cat — that’s not even up for debate. With 16 points already locked in, there’s just not enough room left in the Feral tree for Cat DPS.

I believe the T3.5 gear having so much intellect is a sign that the designers intended to support powershifting. If the design still embraces this playstyle, then that further reinforces the importance of Furor. As for the new TF, the designer’s comment is: “helping players against Bleed immune targets and those not wishing to utilize the Furor talent.” I disagree with that.

Back to the Feral tree — we truly don’t have any spare points to allocate to Open Wounds. The new talent tree leaves us with no room to compromise — all the talents are critical. We sincerely hope the developers will consider our feedback.

content:
No, all idols for resto are mediocre/bad.
You have a choice of 4:
Idol of Health: Reduces the casting time of your Healing Touch spell by 0.15 sec.
Idol of Longevity: Gain 25 mana each time you cast Healing Touch.
Idol of the Forgotten Wilds: Your Regrowth initial healing has a 10% chance to sprout a plant to heal wounded allies for 8 sec.
Idol of Rejuvenation: Increases healing done by Rejuvenation by up to 50.

Rejuv idol is just +60 healing, whilst it heals for ~2800 for me, so yay I guess.
Forgotten Wilds, it scales with your gear, but the targeting and delay is kind of worthless. It heals on average less then 100 per heal, it's around the same as Rejuv idol if you spam mostly regrowth.
Longevity, only thing worth noting, is that on rank 1 healing touch, you regain mana instead of spend it, because it costs 16 and you gain 25. You can spam low ranks forever, even when your OOM. 800 mana max ranks -25 mana is pointless.
Health is kind of okay, when your a healing touch druid.
